data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Control and Protection of “Sensitive Security Information”
extract_result.opi: Personnel and Document Security Division of the Office of Procurement and Property Management
extract_result.purpose: This regulation establishes U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) procedures for identifying unclassified but sensitive information and safeguarding it against unauthorized use or disclosure. The regulation includes minimum protection requirements, including the identification of unclassified but sensitive information as “Sensitive Security Information,” and recommends additional security safeguards to be applied where warranted by the sensitivity of the information.

all offices with custody of the information

policy_statements.source_text: This regulation establishes U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) procedures for identifying unclassified but sensitive information and safeguarding it against unauthorized use or disclosure.

The regulation includes minimum protection requirements, including the identification of unclassified but sensitive information as “Sensitive Security Information,” and recommends additional security safeguards to be applied where warranted by the sensitivity of the information.
This regulation applies to all organizational elements within USDA.
It is the policy of USDA to safeguard unclassified but sensitive security information within its control.
USDA will withhold from release sensitive information that is not appropriate for public disclosure consistent with laws, regulations and court decisions.
policy_statements.target: sensitive information that is not appropriate for public disclosure
conditions: that is not appropriate for public disclosure
consistent with laws, regulations and court decisions

policy_statements.source_text: It is important to note that the Secretary of Agriculture is authorized to originally classify information as “Secret” by order of the President 67 FR 61465 (September 26, 2002).
Therefore, if USDA originates documents that it believes should be classified, Departmental Administration (DA) should be notified as soon as possible.
conditions: if USDA originates documents that it believes should be classified

policy_statements.source_text: Information must not be designated as Sensitive Security Information (SSI) to conceal violations of law; inefficiency; administrative error; prevent embarrassment to a person, organization, department or agency; or restrain competition.

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3080-1 Records Disposition.

The need has arisen to establish formal guidance for all organizational elements outlining procedures for identifying, safeguarding, using, and maintaining the disposition of unclassified information that is considered sensitive security information, such as information pertaining to threats, vulnerabilities, and risks to homeland security and physical security at USDA facilities.

Critical Infrastructure means physical and cyber-based systems, assets (including information whether stored on paper, electronically, or using other means), and services essential to the government or economy of the United States or to a political subdivision thereof, including, but not limited to, systems, facilities, and stockpiles necessary for the operation, maintenance, or distribution of essential goods and services, such as telecommunications (including voice and data transmission and the Internet), electrical power, gas and oil storage, transportation, banking and finance, public health (including biological, chemical, radiological, and other hazardous materials), water supply, waste water, emergency services (including medical, fire, and police services), and the continuity of government operations;

Sensitive Security Information means unclassified information of a sensitive nature, that if publicly disclosed could be expected to have a harmful impact on the security of Federal operations or assets, the public health or safety of the citizens of the United States or its residents, or the nation’s long-term economic prosperity; and which describes, discusses, or reflects:

The ability of any element of the critical infrastructure of the United States to resist intrusion, interference, compromise, theft, or incapacitation by either physical or computer-based attack or other similar conduct that violates Federal, State, or local law; harms interstate, international commerce of the United States; or, threatens public health or safety;

Any currently viable assessment, projection, or estimate of the security vulnerability of any element of the critical infrastructure of the United States, specifically including, but not limited to vulnerability assessment, security testing, risk evaluation, risk-management planning, or risk audit;

Any currently applicable operational problem or solution regarding the security of any element of the critical infrastructure of the United States, specifically including but not limited to the repair, recovery, redesign, reconstruction, relocation, insurance, and continuity of operations of any element;
The following categories are provided for illustration purposes only as examples of the types of information (regardless of format) that may be categorized as SSI:
Physical security status of USDA laboratories, research centers, field facilities, etc., which may also contain vulnerabilities;
Investigative and analytical materials concerning information about physical security at USDA facilities such as the above-named facilities;
Information that could result in physical risk to individuals;
Information that could result in serious damage to critical facilities and/or infrastructures;
Cyber Security Information, which includes, but is not limited to:
Network Drawings or Plans
Program and System Security Plans
Mission Critical and Sensitive Information Technology (IT) Systems and Applications
Capital Planning and Investment Control Data (I-TIPS)
IT Configuration Management Data and Libraries
IT Restricted Space (Drawings, Plans and Equipment Specifications as well as actual space)
Incident and Vulnerability Reports
Risk Assessment Reports, Checklists, Trusted Facilities Manual and Security Users Guide
Cyber Security Policy Guidance and Manual Chapters

Need-to-know means a determination made by an authorized holder of SSI that a prospective recipient requires access to that SSI in order to perform or assist in a lawful and authorized governmental function.
DA Departmental Administration
FOIA Freedom of Information Act
IT Information Technology
OCIO Office of the Chief Information Officer

PA Privacy Act

Under and Assistant Secretaries, Agency Administrators, Regional Directors, Office Directors, and Heads of Field Establishments, hereinafter called Departmental Organizations, will be responsible for the identification and designation of information that warrants protection of SSI.
policy_statements.actor_name: Under and Assistant Secretaries, Agency Administrators, Regional Directors, Office Directors, and Heads of Field Establishments
policy_statements.target: identification and designation of information that warrants protection of SSI

policy_statements.source_text: Heads of Departmental Organizations will:
Specify the categories or types of information, which originate in their organization or are prepared for the use of their organization, and that are designated as SSI.
conditions: which originate in their organization or are prepared for the use of their organization
that are designated as SSI

policy_statements.source_text: The SSI label may be removed from information requested in a FOIA request, if a Departmental Organization Head determines that the information is no longer qualified under the definition provided.
policy_statements.target: information requested in a FOIA request
conditions: if a Departmental Organization Head determines that the information is no longer qualified under the definition provided

policy_statements.source_text: If the sensitivity of the information requires protection in excess of the minimum levels established in this order, the Departmental Organizational Head should ensure that all offices with custody of the information know and comply with such criteria.
policy_statements.target: all offices with custody of the information
conditions: If the sensitivity of the information requires protection in excess of the minimum levels established in this order

policy_statements.source_text: All Departmental Organizations that originate SSI are responsible for conducting reviews, in compliance with DR 3080-01, Records Disposition.
conditions: that originate SSI

policy_statements.source_text: Identify those subordinate officials who have authority to determine which information originating under their supervision or cognizance requires protection against unauthorized disclosure.
The officials so designated are responsible for ensuring that personnel under their direction are aware of information that is considered SSI.
Agencies and Staff Offices will:
Issue directives, if needed, establishing criteria for identifying SSI responsibility within their organizations.
conditions: if needed

policy_statements.source_text: All directives will have prior approval by DA before being finalized and approved.
Ensure that adequate security measures and procedures are implemented to protect SSI.
Ensure that employees of their organizations are aware of their responsibility to protect SSI.
Conduct a risk analysis and determination to identify potential threats and appropriate vulnerabilities to SSI in their custody.
policy_statements.target: potential threats and appropriate vulnerabilities to SSI in their custody

policy_statements.source_text: Determine the potential harm resulting from the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of SSI in their custody.
policy_statements.target: potential harm resulting from the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of SSI in their custody

policy_statements.source_text: Identify appropriate information and designate it as SSI.
Ensure that prompt and appropriate disciplinary action is taken against personnel responsible for unauthorized disclosure of SSI.
policy_statements.target: personnel responsible for unauthorized disclosure of SSI

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental Administration will:
Monitor and ensure compliance with this DR and provide guidance regarding identification and protection of SSI.
The Office of the Chief Information Officer will:
Establish records management disposition policies and procedures to ensure that records designated as SSI are maintained and disposed of according to USDA and Agency records control schedules.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer
policy_statements.target: records management disposition policies and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Partner with DA to ensure wise use is made of existing department resources in terms of security points of contact, security awareness training, and emergency procedures.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer

policy_statements.source_text: Establish USDA policy and standards for IT system protection.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer
policy_statements.target: USDA policy and standards for IT system protection

policy_statements.source_text: System protection functions include encryption, network security products, reliability and security of computing systems, and physical barriers.
OCIO will conduct compliance reviews to ensure that policy and standards are being followed.
Establish strategies and procedures to reconstitute and restore critical information technology infrastructures after serious disruptions.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer
conditions: after serious disruptions

policy_statements.source_text: OCIO will establish programs for restoration of services that includes risk management and consequence management analysis studies and tools, system survivability technologies, back-up and recovery capabilities, and cold/hot site strategies and requirements.
The Office of the General Counsel will:
Provide concurrence prior to responding to any initial FOIA request, Privacy Act (PA) request, or any other request for records involving SSI.
policy_statements.target: any initial FOIA request, Privacy Act (PA) request, or any other request for records involving SSI
conditions: prior to responding to any initial FOIA request, Privacy Act (PA) request, or any other request for records involving SSI

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and Staff Offices should continue to comply with 7 C.F.R. 1.14 with regard to obtaining OGC concurrence when FOIA or PA appeals are denied, but shall also obtain OGC concurrence on any administrative appeal, whether it is granted or denied, for records involving SSI.
conditions: when FOIA or PA appeals are denied
whether it is granted or denied
for records involving SSI

policy_statements.source_text: FOIA requests for access to SSI should be processed as set forth in Section 8f and in accordance with USDA regulations and the Attorney General’s FOIA Memorandum of October 12, 2001, with consideration of all applicable FOIA exemptions, including one or more of the following:
cross_references: Attorney General’s FOIA Memorandum of October 12, 2001

policy_statements.source_text: FOIA Exemptions Potentially Applicable to SSI:
For SSI pertaining to USDA operations or assets, FOIA Exemption 2 should be considered;
conditions: For SSI pertaining to USDA operations or assets

policy_statements.source_text: For current SSI consisting of private sector or industry information submitted voluntarily to USDA that is customarily protected by the submitter, FOIA Exemption 4 should be considered;
conditions: For current SSI consisting of private sector or industry information submitted voluntarily to USDA that is customarily protected by the submitter

policy_statements.source_text: For any SSI the disclosure of which is banned by federal statute, FOIA Exemption 3 should be considered;, and
conditions: For any SSI the disclosure of which is banned by federal statute

policy_statements.source_text: For any SSI that consists of information compiled for law enforcement purposes, FOIA Exemption 7 should be considered.
conditions: For any SSI that consists of information compiled for law enforcement purposes

policy_statements.source_text: USDA material which contains information that the head of the USDA organization has determined requires protection against unauthorized disclosure must be marked in a conspicuous manner with the following notice: “Sensitive Security Information - Disseminate on a Need-to-Know Basis Only.”
The identification of SSI will be done by:
Marking of the SSI notice at the bottom of the front cover (if one is present), the title page (if one is present), the first page, and the outside of the back cover (if one is present);
conditions: if one is present

policy_statements.source_text: Marking of the SSI notice at the top and bottom of every page in a document that contains SSI;
Individual portion markings at the beginning of a paragraph containing SSI shall be done using the acronym SSI;
Notating in a cover memo;

Transmittal documents that have no classified information attached but do have SSI attachments shall have the statement “Sensitive Security Information Attachment - Disseminate on Need-to-Know Basis Only” affixed;
Electronically transmitted messages or data containing SSI shall be preceded by the term “Sensitive Security Information - Disseminate on a Need-to-Know Basis Only” at the beginning of the text;
policy_statements.target: Electronically transmitted messages or data containing SSI

policy_statements.source_text: Inclusion in a category identified as SSI use in an organization directive and known to all personnel handling the information;
All documents that are distributed externally of USDA shall bear the marking on all pages:
“This document contains information which may be exempt from mandatory disclosure under FOIA.
Exemption(s)  apply.”, and
Any other method authorized by DA.
The purpose of identifying SSI is to ensure that all recipients of the material are aware that the information requires protection and should be disseminated on a need-to-know basis only.
The identification method selected should have a minimal effect on the operational efficiency of the organization.
Employees who have custody of material designated as SSI shall exercise due caution to ensure that the information is not available to individuals who have no requirement for it.
conditions: who have custody of material designated as SSI

policy_statements.source_text: At a minimum, individuals who cannot demonstrate a “need-to-know” must not be able to enter areas unescorted or unobserved, and have visual access to SSI.
conditions: who cannot demonstrate a “need-to-know”

policy_statements.source_text: During non-duty hours, SSI shall be afforded, at a minimum, protection of storage in a locked desk or file cabinet, or storage in a facility or area using physical access control measures that afford adequate protection to prevent unauthorized access.
conditions: During non-duty hours

policy_statements.source_text: The sensitivity of some SSI material may require a higher level of protection such as a safe with a combination lock.
SSI stored and processed by an IT facility shall have adequate physical, administrative, and technical safeguards.
policy_statements.target: SSI stored and processed by an IT facility

policy_statements.source_text: Information that has been identified and is known by the recipient as SSI shall be safeguarded from disclosure to unauthorized individuals whether or not the material is physically marked.
policy_statements.target: Information that has been identified and is known by the recipient as SSI
conditions: whether or not the material is physically marked

policy_statements.source_text: Safeguarding from disclosure includes precautions against oral disclosure, prevention of visual access to the information and precautions against release of the material to unauthorized personnel.
SSI leaving the control of the originating organization must be transmitted in a single brown envelope or in a wrapping properly sealed and addressed.
policy_statements.target: SSI leaving the control of the originating organization

policy_statements.source_text: SSI may be transmitted via any form of commercial shipping or U.S. Postal Service method.
SSI may be discussed on the telephone; however, the ease of interception of telephone conversations dictates that discretion be used where the threat of interception exists.
conditions: where the threat of interception exists

policy_statements.source_text: In the latter case, the use of voice privacy equipment or secure telephones should be considered.
conditions: In the latter case

policy_statements.source_text: SSI should not be transmitted or discussed along unsecured pagers, wireless devices or telephone equipment.
These devices are not inherently secure and require additional encryption capabilities before they can be used.
SSI may be transmitted via unclassified fax machines.
However, the sensitivity of the material will determine the need for more secure communications transmission (secure fax).
In the latter case, if the holder is unaware of which method to use, DA or OCIO will provide guidance on the appropriate method of transmission via phone, fax, or IT.
policy_statements.target: appropriate method of transmission via phone, fax, or IT
conditions: In the latter case
if the holder is unaware of which method to use

policy_statements.source_text: The Internet is not secure and therefore should not be used to transmit SSI.
It is critical to safeguard and adequately protect SSI from unlawful or improper disclosure.
OCIO will provide guidance on the appropriate methods of transmission.

SSI that is distributed outside of the Department shall be accompanied by a letter stating that this material is to be treated with the same control measures comparable to the receiving agency’s prescribed measures established comparable to SSI, that at a minimum meet our security control measures (Sensitive But Unclassified, Limited Official Use Only, For Official Use Only, etc.).
policy_statements.target: SSI that is distributed outside of the Department

The need has arisen to establish formal guidance for all organizational elements outlining procedures for identifying, safeguarding, using, and maintaining the disposition of unclassified information that is considered sensitive security information, such as information pertaining to threats, vulnerabilities, and risks to homeland security and physical security at USDA facilities.

Critical Infrastructure  means physical and cyber-based systems, assets (including information whether stored on paper, electronically, or using other means), and services essential to the government or economy of the United States or to a political subdivision thereof, including, but not limited to, systems, facilities, and stockpiles necessary for the operation, maintenance, or distribution of essential goods and services, such as telecommunications (including voice and data transmission and the Internet), electrical power, gas and oil storage, transportation, banking and finance, public health (including biological, chemical, radiological, and other hazardous materials), water supply, waste water, emergency services (including medical, fire, and police services), and the continuity of government operations;

Sensitive Security Information  means unclassified information of a sensitive nature, that if publicly disclosed could be expected to have a harmful impact on the security of Federal operations or assets, the public health or safety of the citizens of the United States or its residents, or the nation’s long-term economic prosperity; and which describes, discusses, or reflects:

The ability of any element of the critical infrastructure of the United States to resist intrusion, interference, compromise, theft, or incapacitation by either physical or computer-based attack or other similar conduct that violates Federal, State, or local law; harms interstate, international commerce of the United States; or, threatens public health or safety;

Any currently viable assessment, projection, or estimate of the security vulnerability of any element of the critical infrastructure of the United States, specifically including, but not limited to vulnerability assessment, security testing, risk evaluation, risk-management planning, or risk audit;

Any currently applicable operational problem or solution regarding the security of any element of the critical infrastructure of the United States, specifically including but not limited to the repair, recovery, redesign, reconstruction, relocation, insurance, and continuity of operations of any element;
The following categories are provided for illustration purposes only as examples of the types of information (regardless of format) that may be categorized as SSI:
Physical security status of USDA laboratories, research centers, field facilities, etc., which may also contain vulnerabilities;
Investigative and analytical materials concerning information about physical security at USDA facilities such as the above-named facilities;
Information that could result in physical risk to individuals;
Information that could result in serious damage to critical facilities and/or infrastructures;
Cyber Security Information, which includes, but is not limited to:
Mission Critical and Sensitive Information Technology (IT) Systems and Applications
Capital Planning and Investment Control Data (I-TIPS)
IT Configuration Management Data and Libraries
IT Restricted Space (Drawings, Plans and Equipment Specifications as well as actual space)
Risk Assessment Reports, Checklists, Trusted Facilities Manual and Security Users Guide
Cyber Security Policy Guidance and Manual Chapters
